title: Rising Academies' WhatsApp math tutor Rori: in a school-assigned trial in 11 Ghanaian schools, the authors report a 0.36 effect size from February to August 2023 (arXiv 2024)
summary: In a preprint coauthored by Rising Academies staff, Ghanaian students who used its WhatsApp tutor Rori one hour a week in 2023 gained 0.36 standard deviations more in math than controls.
account: Rori is an AI-powered conversational math tutor on WhatsApp, created by Rising Academies, an education network that runs schools in Ghana. Henkel (University of Oxford), Horne-Robinson (Rising Academies), Kozhakhmetova and Lee (J-PAL North America) report a preliminary evaluation in 11 Rising Academies schools in Ghana. The schools were randomly assigned at the school level, five to treatment and six to control. Students in grades 3–8 took a 35-question math assessment in early February 2023 (baseline) and late August 2023 (endline). Of the 637 students who took the baseline (336 treatment, 301 control), 477 took the endline. Treated students were given a phone for one hour a week during study hall to study math with Rori. Controls continued regular instruction. The first version of the preprint appeared on arXiv on 15 February 2024. In the second version, posted on 5 May 2024, the authors report an effect size of 0.36 (Cohen's d, p < 0.001) and a marginal cost of about $5 per student. The arXiv abstract still describes approximately 1,000 students in grades 3–9, two 30-minute sessions a week over 8 months and an effect size of 0.37. These figures do not match the body of the second version. In December 2024 a University of Ghana professor and two Rising Academies staff registered a 2025 follow-up pilot in government and low-cost private schools. The registry entry posts no results. By May 2026 Rising Academies reported that it was piloting Rori in government schools in Ghana's Eastern Region with World Bank support. It had extended the pilot by six months and was preparing a larger randomized trial in more than 100 public schools from September 2026.

headline: Rising Academies' WhatsApp tutor Rori raises math scores in Ghana

comparator.against: control-group students at schools without Rori access who continued regular math instruction

comparator.after: treatment group growth score M = 5.13 (SD = 7.03), an effect size of 0.36 (Cohen's d)
comparator.quote: An independent samples t-test between the control (M = 2.12, SD = 6.30) and the treatment group (M = 5.13, SD = 7.03) revealed that the 3.01 difference in growth scores was highly statistically significant (p < 0.001).

later.quote: With World Bank support, Rising is piloting Rori, our AI-enabled virtual maths tutor, in government schools in Ghana’s Eastern Region. display.answer: Both versions of the preprint come from authors at the University of Oxford, Rising Academies and J-PAL North America, so the vendor coauthored them. The registry entry of 4 December 2024 lists two Rising Academies staff with a University of Ghana investigator, and the news post of 6 May 2026 is Rising Academies' own. No source independent of the makers reports the result.
The geopolitical implications are unclear.

fields.summary: In a preprint coauthored by Rising Academies staff, Ghanaian students who used its WhatsApp tutor Rori one hour a week in 2023 gained 0.36 standard deviations more in math than controls.
fields.account: Rori is an AI-powered conversational math tutor on WhatsApp, created by Rising Academies, an education network that runs schools in Ghana. Henkel (University of Oxford), Horne-Robinson (Rising Academies), Kozhakhmetova and Lee (J-PAL North America) report a preliminary evaluation in 11 Rising Academies schools in Ghana. The schools were randomly assigned at the school level, five to treatment and six to control. Students in grades 3–8 took a 35-question math assessment in early February 2023 (baseline) and late August 2023 (endline). Of the 637 students who took the baseline (336 treatment, 301 control), 477 took the endline. Treated students were given a phone for one hour a week during study hall to study math with Rori. Controls continued regular instruction. The first version of the preprint appeared on arXiv on 15 February 2024. In the second version, posted on 5 May 2024, the authors report an effect size of 0.36 (Cohen's d, p < 0.001) and a marginal cost of about $5 per student. The arXiv abstract still describes approximately 1,000 students in grades 3–9, two 30-minute sessions a week over 8 months and an effect size of 0.37. These figures do not match the body of the second version. In December 2024 a University of Ghana professor and two Rising Academies staff registered a 2025 follow-up pilot in government and low-cost private schools. The registry entry posts no results. By May 2026 Rising Academies reported that it was piloting Rori in government schools in Ghana's Eastern Region with World Bank support. It had extended the pilot by six months and was preparing a larger randomized trial in more than 100 public schools from September 2026.
